title: GloCOM: A Short Text Neural Topic Model via Global Clustering Context
subcategory: neural short-text topic model with PLM-based cluster aggregation
task: Short-text topic modelling (topics and per-document topic proportions)
problem: Short texts suffer from data sparsity (few word co-occurrences) and label sparsity (incomplete reconstruction targets); existing aggregation is slow, low quality, or loses per-document proportions.
architecture: Short texts are clustered with PLM sentence embeddings; texts in a cluster are concatenated into a global document; a VAE-based NTM infers a global topic distribution per cluster and a local distribution per text (global distribution plus learnable noise); each text's reconstruction target is augmented with its global document; topics are built from word and topic embeddings with ECR regularisation.
llm_or_encoder: all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (default) for clustering; other embedding models compared
key_results: SearchSnippets, K = 50: Purity 0.806 and NMI 0.502 vs 0.711 and 0.419 for ECRTM.
strengths: Keeps individual document-topic proportions while benefiting from aggregation.
Global-context augmentation of the reconstruction target addresses label sparsity directly.

limitations.text: The number of clusters used to build global documents must be chosen in advance.
Reliance on PLM clustering makes dynamic or real-time use difficult.

notes: K = 50 and 100; kNNTM re-implemented by the authors.
